title: Geometry
description: GeoJSON subset (RFC 7946) used for targets and footprints. A subset rather than full GeoJSON: we accept Point and Polygon only. Accepting GeometryCollection or MultiPolygon would mean the feasibility sweep has to handle disjoint targets, which is a real feature with real scheduling consequences (one request, multiple non-adjacent acquisitions) and is out of scope. Rejecting them at the contract boundary is honest; silently mishandling them would not be.

Position.description: GeoJSON position: [longitude, latitude]. Longitude first. This ordering trips up everyone at least once, which is why it is stated here and asserted in a contract test rather than left to memory. Altitude is not accepted — targets are on the ellipsoid.

LinearRing.description: Closed ring: the last position must equal the first. JSON Schema cannot express that, so the adapter checks it. Minimum four positions because a closed triangle needs four.

coordinates.description: First ring is the exterior boundary, subsequent rings are holes. Exterior counter-clockwise, holes clockwise, per RFC 7946.

TargetGeometry.description: What the customer wants imaged. A Point is treated as a zero-area target and satisfied by any acquisition whose footprint contains it. A Polygon must be fully contained by a single acquisition footprint — partial coverage across multiple passes is a mosaicking feature, and it is out of scope.

BoundingBox.description: [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees, WGS84. Used only for read-model queries and viewport filtering, never as a target.
